title: Error Messages with ?
story: Your users are confused. When something goes wrong, they just see 'Error.' They need to know what happened and how to fix it. Time to write error messages that actually help.
why: Custom error messages make programs user-friendly — instead of cryptic failures, users get actionable feedback on exactly what went wrong.
analogy: Good error messages are like GPS recalculating — they don't just say 'wrong turn,' they tell you where you are and how to get back on track.
try_it: Write a `validate_date(day: Int, month: Int) -> Result[Str, Str]` function. Validate: day 1-31, month 1-12. Then add a check for February (month 2, max day 28). Write separate error messages for each failure. Test February 29th, April 31st, and month 13.
tips: Write error messages that tell the user what they did wrong AND what's expected
Check the most common errors first — empty input and boundary violations
Use string concatenation in errors to include the user's actual input: 'Got X, expected Y'
common_mistakes: Writing error messages that are too vague — 'Invalid input' doesn't help anyone
Putting all validation in one big if-else chain — extract validators into named functions
Returning Ok with a warning message — if it's a warning, use Ok; if it's an error, use Err
